run_trial() {  # run_trial <jid> <arm> <task> <type> <kind> <trial> <run_id> <task_yaml> <watchdog_s>
  local jid="$1" arm="$2" task="$3" type="$4" kind="$5" trial="$6" rid="$7" tyaml="$8" wds="$9"
  local base="$BATCH_DIR/$arm/$task-t$trial" tlog="$BATCH_DIR/$arm/$task-t$trial.log"
  local attempt=0 rd="" st="" prc retry_reason="" first_usd=0 sig override="" pid
  local t0 t1
  mkdir -p "$BATCH_DIR/$arm"
  t0="$(date +%s)"
  while [[ $attempt -lt 2 ]]; do
    attempt=$((attempt + 1))
    rd="$(fresh_dir "$base")"
    printf '%s\n' "$rd" > "$JOBS_DIR/$jid.rundir"
    rm -f "$JOBS_DIR/$jid.wd" "$JOBS_DIR/$jid.wdkill"
    printf '%s run-ablation: %s attempt %d run_dir %s\n' "$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)" "$rid" "$attempt" "$rd" >> "$tlog"
    local -a cmd=("$PIPELINE_BIN" --task-yaml "$tyaml" --arm "$arm" --run-dir "$rd" --run-id "$rid" --trial "$trial"
                  --source-tree "$TREE" --suite-file "$SUITE_FILE" --executor "$EXECUTOR" --image "$IMAGE"
                  --docker-bin "$DOCKER_BIN" --max-run-usd "$RUN_CAP")
    # its own process group, so the watchdog can signal the pipeline and everything under it
    if command -v setsid >/dev/null 2>&1; then setsid "${cmd[@]}" >> "$tlog" 2>&1 < /dev/null &
    else "${cmd[@]}" >> "$tlog" 2>&1 < /dev/null &
    fi
    pid=$!
    printf '%s %s %s\n' "$pid" "$(date +%s)" "$wds" > "$JOBS_DIR/$jid.pgid"
    prc=0; wait "$pid" || prc=$?
    rm -f "$JOBS_DIR/$jid.pgid"
    st="$(final_status "$rd")"
    if [[ -f "$JOBS_DIR/$jid.wd" ]]; then
      override=interrupted
      synthesize_record "$rd" "$arm" "$task" "$type" "$trial" "$rid" "watchdog: no final pipeline record after ${wds}s (pipeline exit $prc)"
      break
    fi
    if [[ -z "$st" ]]; then
      override=interrupted
      synthesize_record "$rd" "$arm" "$task" "$type" "$trial" "$rid" "no final pipeline record (pipeline exit $prc)"
      break
    fi
    if [[ "$st" == agent_error ]] && sig="$(is_pipeline_transport_failure "$rd")"; then
      if [[ $attempt -lt 2 ]]; then
        first_usd="$(jq -r '(.spent_usd // 0) | tonumber? // 0' "$rd/meta/pipeline.json" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)"
        retry_reason="transport: ${sig% *} in phase ${sig#* }"
        printf '%s run-ablation: %s %s; retrying once after %ss into a fresh run dir\n' "$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)" "$rid" "$retry_reason" "$RETRY_WAIT" >> "$tlog"
        sleep "$RETRY_WAIT"; continue
      fi
      override=transport_error
    fi
    break
  done
  post_run "$rd" "$rid" "$task" "$tyaml" "$attempt" "$retry_reason" "$st" "$override" "$JOBS_DIR/$jid.row" "$tlog"
  t1="$(date +%s)"
  jq -n --arg rid "$rid" --arg rd "$rd" --argjson att "$attempt" --arg rr "$retry_reason" --arg first "$first_usd" \
    --arg pst "${st:-}" --arg ov "$PR_OVERRIDE" --arg te "$PR_TE" --arg ter "$PR_TE_REASON" --argjson drift "$PR_DRIFT" \
    --argjson grc "$PR_GRC" --argjson rrc "$PR_RRC" --argjson secs "$(( t1 - t0 ))" --argjson extra "$PR_EXTRA" \
    '{run_id: $rid, run_dir: $rd, attempts: $att, retry_reason: (if $rr == "" then null else $rr end),
      first_attempt_usd: ($first | tonumber? // 0), pipeline_status: $pst, override: $ov, took_effect: $te,
      took_effect_reason: $ter, drift: $drift, grade_rc: $grc, row_rc: $rrc, seconds: $secs,
      extra_models: $extra}' > "$JOBS_DIR/$jid.result.tmp"
  mv "$JOBS_DIR/$jid.result.tmp" "$JOBS_DIR/$jid.result"
}

# --- parent: collect a finished job ---------------------------------------------------
append_and_validate() {  # append_and_validate <row-file> <run_id> → 0 ok; 1 invalid (ROWS_INVALID set)
  local rowf="$1" rid="$2" vout vrc=0 n
  local -a v=("$ROW_BIN" --validate "$ROWS"); [[ "$SMOKE" == true ]] && v+=(--allow-ungraded)
  if command -v flock >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    { flock -x 9; cat "$rowf" >> "$ROWS"; vout="$("${v[@]}" 2>&1)" || vrc=$?; } 9>>"$ROWS.lock"
  else
    cat "$rowf" >> "$ROWS"; vout="$("${v[@]}" 2>&1)" || vrc=$?
  fi
  n="$(grep -cF "\"run_id\":\"$rid\"" "$ROWS" || true)"
  if [[ $vrc -ne 0 ]]; then
    ROWS_INVALID="$(jq -cn --arg r "$rid" --arg e "$(printf '%s' "$vout" | tail -1)" '{run_id: $r, error: $e}')"; return 1
  fi
  if [[ "$n" -ne 1 ]]; then
    ROWS_INVALID="$(jq -cn --arg r "$rid" --argjson n "$n" '{run_id: $r, error: "run_id rowed \($n) times"}')"; return 1
  fi
  return 0
}

# apply_flags <arm> <run_id> <took_effect> <reason> <drift> — a took-effect FAIL pauses the
# arm (DEC-0418); the first drift stops the batch (DEC-0407)
apply_flags() {
  if [[ "$3" == fail ]] && ! is_paused "$1"; then
    PAUSED_JSON="$(jq -c --arg a "$1" --arg why "$2: $4" '. + {($a): $why}' <<<"$PAUSED_JSON")"
    log "PAUSED arm $1: $4 (no further trial of $1 launches until --resume --clear-arm $1)"
  fi
  if [[ "$5" != null && "$DRIFT_JSON" == null ]]; then
    DRIFT_JSON="$5"; STOP=drift
    log "DRIFT $2: $5; no further trial launches; the batch fails when the running trials end (DEC-0407)"
  fi
  return 0
}
# record_extra <run_id> <extra models json> — the run's extra models replace its earlier entry
record_extra() {
  EXTRA_RUNS_JSON="$(jq -c --arg r "$1" --argjson e "$2" \
    'if ($e | type) == "object" and ($e | length) > 0 then .[$r] = ($e | map_values(.output_tokens // 0)) else del(.[$r]) end' <<<"$EXTRA_RUNS_JSON")"
}

# outage_tick <run_id> <row status, empty without a row> — the breaker (DEC-0554): consecutive
# collected transport_error trials (collection order, any arm) trip it at $OUTAGE_BREAKER (0 off)
outage_tick() {
  if [[ "$2" == transport_error ]]; then OUTAGE_RUN=$((OUTAGE_RUN + 1)); else OUTAGE_RUN=0; fi
  if [[ "$OUTAGE_BREAKER" -gt 0 && $OUTAGE_RUN -ge $OUTAGE_BREAKER && "$OUTAGE_JSON" == null && -z "$STOP" ]]; then
    STOP=outage
    OUTAGE_JSON="$(jq -cn --arg at "$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)" --argjson n "$OUTAGE_RUN" --arg r "$1" \
      '{at: $at, consecutive: $n, last_run_id: $r,
        message: "partial (outage breaker): \($n) consecutive transport failures; --resume --rerun-status transport_error after the network is back"}')"
    log "OUTAGE breaker: $OUTAGE_RUN consecutive transport_error trials (last $1); no further trial launches (DEC-0554)"
  fi
  return 0
}

collect() {  # collect <jid> <plan-index>
  local jid="$1" k="$2" arm="${PL_ARM[$2]}" rid="${PL_RUN[$2]}" kind="${PL_KIND[$2]}" res="$JOBS_DIR/$1.result"
  if [[ ! -f "$res" ]]; then
    SPENT="$(fadd "$SPENT" "$RUN_CAP")"; ASSUMED_CAP=$((ASSUMED_CAP + 1))
    log "FAILED $rid (the trial job ended without a result; see $BATCH_DIR/$arm/${PL_TASK[$k]}-t${PL_TRIAL[$k]}.log); assumed cap: USD $RUN_CAP charged to spent"
    outage_tick "$rid" ""
    rm -f "$JOBS_DIR/$jid".*; write_status; return 0
  fi
  local first att rr te ter drift
  first="$(jq -r '.first_attempt_usd' "$res")" att="$(jq -r '.attempts' "$res")" rr="$(jq -r '.retry_reason // ""' "$res")"
  te="$(jq -r '.took_effect' "$res")" ter="$(jq -r '.took_effect_reason' "$res")" drift="$(jq -c '.drift' "$res")"
  record_extra "$rid" "$(jq -c '.extra_models // {}' "$res")"
  if [[ "$att" -ge 2 ]]; then
    RETRIES_JSON="$(jq -c --arg r "$rid" --arg why "$rr" --arg u "$first" '. + [{run_id: $r, reason: $why, first_attempt_usd: ($u | tonumber)}]' <<<"$RETRIES_JSON")"
    SPENT="$(fadd "$SPENT" "$first")"; LEDGER_USD="$(fadd "$LEDGER_USD" "$first")"
  fi
  local st="" cost deg pass
  if [[ -s "$JOBS_DIR/$jid.row" ]]; then
    IFS=$'\t' read -r st cost deg pass < <(jq -r '[.status, ((.cost_usd // 0) | tostring), ((.degraded // false) | tostring),
        ((.hidden_test_pass_rate // .defect_catch_rate // "n/a") | tostring)] | @tsv' "$JOBS_DIR/$jid.row")
    if is_rerun "$rid"; then
      # DEC-0553: the new row replaces the old one in place; the old row's reported cost moves to the ledger
      if replace_row_try "$rid" "$JOBS_DIR/$jid.row"; then
        local from ocost
        from="$(jq -r --arg r "$rid" '.[$r].status' <<<"$RERUN_OLD")" ocost="$(jq -r --arg r "$rid" '.[$r].cost' <<<"$RERUN_OLD")"
        LEDGER_USD="$(fadd "$LEDGER_USD" "$ocost")"
        RERUN_LIST="${RERUN_LIST/$'\n'"$rid"$'\n'/$'\n'}"
        RERUN_JSON="$(jq -c --arg r "$rid" --arg f "$from" --arg t "$st" --arg c "$ocost" --arg at "$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)" \
          '. + [{run_id: $r, from: $f, to: $t, old_cost_usd: ($c | tonumber), at: $at}]' <<<"$RERUN_JSON")"
        log "rerun $rid: $from → $st (row replaced in place)"
      else
        ROWS_INVALID="$(jq -cn --arg r "$rid" --arg e "$REPLACE_ERR" '{run_id: $r, error: ("rerun replacement: " + $e)}')"
        log "ROWS INVALID after $rid: $(jq -r '.error' <<<"$ROWS_INVALID")"; STOP=invalid
      fi
    elif append_and_validate "$JOBS_DIR/$jid.row" "$rid"; then :; else
      log "ROWS INVALID after $rid: $(jq -r '.error' <<<"$ROWS_INVALID")"; STOP=invalid
    fi
    DONE_LIST="$DONE_LIST$rid"$'\n'
    account_row "$arm" "$kind" "$rid" "$st" "$cost" "$deg"
    log "done $rid $st pass=$pass USD $cost $(( $(jq -r '.seconds' "$res") / 60 ))m attempts $att${rr:+ ($rr)}"
  else
    SPENT="$(fadd "$SPENT" "$RUN_CAP")"; ASSUMED_CAP=$((ASSUMED_CAP + 1))
    log "FAILED $rid: no row written (ablation-row.sh exit $(jq -r '.row_rc' "$res"); see the trial log); assumed cap: USD $RUN_CAP charged to spent"
  fi
  outage_tick "$rid" "$st"
  apply_flags "$arm" "$rid" "$te" "$ter" "$drift"
  rm -f "$JOBS_DIR/$jid".*
  write_status
}

PIDS=() PJOB=() PIDX=()
watchdog_tick() {
  local j f pid start wds now rd t0
  now="$(date +%s)"
  for j in ${PJOB[@]+"${PJOB[@]}"}; do
    f="$JOBS_DIR/$j.pgid"; [[ -f "$f" ]] || continue
    read -r pid start wds < "$f" 2>/dev/null || continue
    [[ -n "$WATCHDOG_OVERRIDE" ]] && wds="$WATCHDOG_OVERRIDE"
    [[ $(( now - start )) -gt $wds ]] || continue
    rd="$(cat "$JOBS_DIR/$j.rundir" 2>/dev/null || true)"
    [[ -z "$(final_status "$rd")" ]] || continue
    if [[ ! -f "$JOBS_DIR/$j.wd" ]]; then
      printf '%s\n' "$now" > "$JOBS_DIR/$j.wd"
      log "watchdog: $j has no final pipeline record after ${wds}s (twice its phase-sum timeout); SIGTERM to process group $pid"
      kill -TERM -- "-$pid" 2>/dev/null || kill -TERM "$pid" 2>/dev/null || true
    elif [[ ! -f "$JOBS_DIR/$j.wdkill" ]]; then
      read -r t0 < "$JOBS_DIR/$j.wd" || t0="$now"
      if [[ $(( now - t0 )) -ge $WATCHDOG_GRACE ]]; then
        : > "$JOBS_DIR/$j.wdkill"
        log "watchdog: $j still running ${WATCHDOG_GRACE}s after SIGTERM; SIGKILL to process group $pid"
        kill -KILL -- "-$pid" 2>/dev/null || kill -KILL "$pid" 2>/dev/null || true
      fi
    fi
  done
  return 0
}
reap() {  # reap until fewer than $1 jobs run
  local i
  while [[ ${#PIDS[@]} -ge $1 ]]; do
    for i in "${!PIDS[@]}"; do
      if ! kill -0 "${PIDS[$i]}" 2>/dev/null; then
        wait "${PIDS[$i]}" 2>/dev/null || true
        collect "${PJOB[$i]}" "${PIDX[$i]}"
        unset 'PIDS[i]' 'PJOB[i]' 'PIDX[i]'
        PIDS=("${PIDS[@]+"${PIDS[@]}"}"); PJOB=("${PJOB[@]+"${PJOB[@]}"}"); PIDX=("${PIDX[@]+"${PIDX[@]}"}")
        break
      fi
    done
    watchdog_tick
    [[ ${#PIDS[@]} -ge $1 ]] && sleep "$POLL_S"
  done
  return 0
}

on_signal() {
  SIGNALLED=true
  log "interrupted: the driver received a signal; running trials are signalled and will be rerun by --resume"
  STATE=partial; write_status
  exit 1
}

finish() {  # finish <state> <exit> <message>
  STATE="$1"; write_status; log "$3"
  local line
  line="$("$SPEND_BIN" 2>/dev/null | tail -1 || true)"
  {
    printf '%s %s\n' "$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)" "${line:-spend.sh printed nothing}"
    printf '%s batch %s spend USD %s (rows %s + first attempts %s; %s assumed cap charge(s)); max %s\n' \
      "$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)" "$BATCH" "$SPENT" "$ROWS_USD" "$LEDGER_USD" "$ASSUMED_CAP" "${MAX_USD:-none}"
  } >> "$BATCH_DIR/spend.txt"
  echo "run-ablation: $3"
  echo "batch: $BATCH_DIR"
  exit "$2"
}

# --- --rerow: the post-run chain again over a rowed run dir, the row replaced in place ---
# replace_row_try <run_id> <new-row-file> → 0 replaced; 1 with REPLACE_ERR set and the rows file
# untouched (the old row stays). replace_row is the --rerow form: it dies instead
replace_row_try() {
  local rid="$1" newf="$2" tmp="$ROWS.rerow.$$" rc=0 vout="" perr
  REPLACE_ERR=""
  local -a v=("$ROW_BIN" --validate "$tmp"); [[ "$SMOKE" == true ]] && v+=(--allow-ungraded)
  {
    command -v flock >/dev/null 2>&1 && flock -x 9
    perr="$(python3 -I - "$ROWS" "$tmp" "$BATCH" "$rid" "$newf" 2>&1 <<'PY'
import json, sys
rows, tmp, batch, rid, newf = sys.argv[1:6]
new = open(newf, encoding="utf-8").read().strip()
out, n = [], 0
with open(rows, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
    for line in fh:
        try: o = json.loads(line)
        except ValueError: o = None
        if isinstance(o, dict) and o.get("batch") == batch and o.get("run_id") == rid:
            n += 1; out.append(new + "\n")
        else:
            out.append(line if line.endswith("\n") else line + "\n")
if n != 1:
    print("run_id %s has %d rows" % (rid, n), file=sys.stderr); sys.exit(1)
with open(tmp, "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh: fh.writelines(out)
PY
)" || rc=$?
    if [[ $rc -eq 0 ]]; then
      vout="$("${v[@]}" 2>&1)" || rc=$?
      if [[ $rc -eq 0 ]]; then mv "$tmp" "$ROWS"; else REPLACE_ERR="$(printf '%s\n' "$vout" | tail -1)"; fi
    else
      REPLACE_ERR="$(printf '%s\n' "$perr" | tail -1)"
    fi
  } 9>>"$ROWS.lock"
  rm -f "$tmp"
  [[ $rc -eq 0 ]] || { REPLACE_ERR="${REPLACE_ERR:-exit $rc}"; return 1; }
  return 0
}
replace_row() {  # replace_row <run_id> <new-row-file> → 0 replaced; dies (rows file untouched) otherwise
  replace_row_try "$1" "$2" && return 0
  printf '%s\n' "$REPLACE_ERR" >&2
  die "rerow $1: the replacement did not validate or the row moved ($REPLACE_ERR); $ROWS unchanged"
}
rerow_all() {
  local n k rid arm task trial rd tlog newst
  for n in "${!RR_K[@]}"; do
    k="${RR_K[$n]}" rid="${PL_RUN[${RR_K[$n]}]}" arm="${PL_ARM[${RR_K[$n]}]}" task="${PL_TASK[${RR_K[$n]}]}"
    trial="${PL_TRIAL[${RR_K[$n]}]}" rd="${RR_RD[$n]}" tlog="$BATCH_DIR/$arm/$task-t$trial.log"
    printf '%s run-ablation: rerow %s run_dir %s (was %s)\n' "$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)" "$rid" "$rd" "${RR_FROM[$n]}" >> "$tlog"
    rm -f "$WORK/rerow-$n.row"
    post_run "$rd" "$rid" "$task" "${PL_YAML[$k]}" "${RR_ATT[$n]}" "${RR_REASON[$n]}" "$(final_status "$rd")" "" "$WORK/rerow-$n.row" "$tlog"
    [[ -s "$WORK/rerow-$n.row" ]] || die "rerow $rid: ablation-row.sh wrote no row (exit $PR_RRC; see $tlog); $ROWS unchanged"
    replace_row "$rid" "$WORK/rerow-$n.row"
    newst="$(jq -r '.status' "$WORK/rerow-$n.row")"
    record_extra "$rid" "$PR_EXTRA"
    apply_flags "$arm" "$rid" "$PR_TE" "$PR_TE_REASON" "$PR_DRIFT"
    REROWED_JSON="$(jq -c --arg r "$rid" --arg f "${RR_FROM[$n]}" --arg t "$newst" --arg at "$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)" \
      '. + [{run_id: $r, from: $f, to: $t, at: $at}]' <<<"$REROWED_JSON")"
    jq --argjson r "$REROWED_JSON" '.rerowed = $r' "$BATCH_DIR/STATUS.json" > "$BATCH_DIR/STATUS.json.tmp" \
      && mv "$BATCH_DIR/STATUS.json.tmp" "$BATCH_DIR/STATUS.json"
    log "rerow $rid: ${RR_FROM[$n]} → $newst"
  done
  return 0
}

# --- --resume reconciliation: rows on disk are the truth (after --rerow) --------
if [[ "$RESUME" == true ]]; then
  ST_PATH="$BATCH_DIR/STATUS.json"
  STARTED="$(jq -r '.started // empty' "$ST_PATH")"; [[ -n "$STARTED" ]] || STARTED="$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)"
  CUTS_JSON="$(jq -c '.cuts // []' "$ST_PATH")"; RETRIES_JSON="$(jq -c '.retries // []' "$ST_PATH")"
  PAUSED_JSON="$(jq -c '.paused_arms // {}' "$ST_PATH")"
  LEDGER_USD="$(jq -r '.spend.ledger_usd // 0' "$ST_PATH")"; SPENT="$(fadd "$SPENT" "$LEDGER_USD")"
  EXTRA_RUNS_JSON="$(jq -c '.extra_models_by_run // {} | if type == "object" then . else {} end' "$ST_PATH")"
  DRIFT_CLEARED_JSON="$(jq -c '.drift_cleared // []' "$ST_PATH")"; REROWED_JSON="$(jq -c '.rerowed // []' "$ST_PATH")"
  RERUN_JSON="$(jq -c '.rerun // []' "$ST_PATH")"
  OUTAGE_HISTORY_JSON="$(jq -c '.outage_history // []' "$ST_PATH")"
  if [[ "$(jq -c '.outage // null' "$ST_PATH")" != null ]]; then
    OUTAGE_HISTORY_JSON="$(jq -c --argjson o "$(jq -c '.outage' "$ST_PATH")" '. + [$o]' <<<"$OUTAGE_HISTORY_JSON")"
    log "resume: the outage breaker record $(jq -c '.outage' "$ST_PATH") is cleared (kept under outage_history)"
  fi
  if [[ "$CLEAR_PENDING" != null ]]; then
    DRIFT_CLEARED_JSON="$(jq -c --argjson c "$CLEAR_PENDING" '. + [$c]' <<<"$DRIFT_CLEARED_JSON")"
    log "resume: --clear-drift $(jq -r '.run_id' <<<"$CLEAR_PENDING") (previous drift re-read under the current rule: none)"
  fi
  for a in ${CLEAR_ARMS[@]+"${CLEAR_ARMS[@]}"}; do
    if is_paused "$a"; then PAUSED_JSON="$(jq -c --arg a "$a" 'del(.[$a])' <<<"$PAUSED_JSON")"; log "resume: --clear-arm $a (paused arm released)"
    else log "resume: --clear-arm $a: the arm is not paused"; fi
  done
  # rerows first, so spend and per_arm below come from the final rows
  rerow_all
  if [[ -f "$ROWS" ]]; then
    dup="$(jq -R -r --arg b "$BATCH" 'fromjson? | select(type == "object" and .batch == $b) | .run_id' "$ROWS" | sort | uniq -d | head -3 | tr '\n' ' ')"
    [[ -z "$dup" ]] || refuse "resume: $ROWS holds run_id(s) twice: $dup"
    want_ids=$'\n'; for r in ${RERUN_IDS[@]+"${RERUN_IDS[@]}"}; do want_ids="$want_ids$r"$'\n'; done
    rerow_ids=$'\n'; for r in ${REROW_IDS[@]+"${REROW_IDS[@]}"}; do rerow_ids="$rerow_ids$r"$'\n'; done
    want_st=" ${RERUN_STATUSES[*]+"${RERUN_STATUSES[*]}"} "
    while IFS=$'\t' read -r rid st cost deg; do
      k=-1
      for j in "${!PL_RUN[@]}"; do [[ "${PL_RUN[$j]}" == "$rid" ]] && { k=$j; break; }; done
      [[ $k -ge 0 ]] || continue
      if [[ "$want_ids" == *$'\n'"$rid"$'\n'* ]] \
         || { [[ "$want_st" == *" $st "* ]] && [[ "$rerow_ids" != *$'\n'"$rid"$'\n'* ]]; }; then
        # DEC-0553: out of the done set, so the plan launches it again; no counter, no assumed charge;
        # its reported cost (real spend) stays in spent
        [[ "$cost" =~ ^[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?([eE][-+]?[0-9]+)?$ ]] || cost=0
        RERUN_LIST="$RERUN_LIST$rid"$'\n'; SPENT="$(fadd "$SPENT" "$cost")"
        RERUN_OLD="$(jq -c --arg r "$rid" --arg s "$st" --arg c "$cost" '.[$r] = {status: $s, cost: ($c | tonumber)}' <<<"$RERUN_OLD")"
        continue
      fi
      DONE_LIST="$DONE_LIST$rid"$'\n'
      i="$(arm_index "${PL_ARM[$k]}")"; C_LAUNCHED[$i]=$(( ${C_LAUNCHED[$i]} + 1 )); LAUNCHED=$((LAUNCHED + 1))
      account_row "${PL_ARM[$k]}" "${PL_KIND[$k]}" "$rid" "$st" "$cost" "$deg"
    done < <(jq -R -r --arg b "$BATCH" 'fromjson? | select(type == "object" and .batch == $b)
               | [.run_id, .status, ((.cost_usd // 0) | tostring), ((.degraded // false) | tostring)] | @tsv' "$ROWS")
  fi
  n_rerun="$(printf '%s' "$RERUN_LIST" | grep -c . || true)"
  [[ ${#RERUN_STATUSES[@]} -eq 0 && ${#RERUN_IDS[@]} -eq 0 ]] \
    || log "resume: $n_rerun trial(s) flagged for a rerun (--rerun ${RERUN_IDS[*]+"${RERUN_IDS[*]}"} --rerun-status ${RERUN_STATUSES[*]+"${RERUN_STATUSES[*]}"}; DEC-0553)"
  log "resume: batch $BATCH, $LAUNCHED of $PLAN_N trials rowed, spent $SPENT, paused $(jq -c 'keys' <<<"$PAUSED_JSON")"
fi

# --- dispatch --------------------------------------------------------------------------
log "start batch=$BATCH smoke=$SMOKE source=${SRC_FULL:0:12} executor=$EXECUTOR image=$IMAGE cli=$CLI_VERSION concurrency=$CONCURRENCY rows=$ROWS"
log "$PLAN_LINE"
[[ "$RESUME" == true ]] || jq -r '.refused[] | "refused: \(.arm) \(.task_id) \(.type) (task_types \(.task_types | tojson)) DEC-0405"' "$WORK/plan.json" \
  | while IFS= read -r l; do log "$l"; done
write_status
trap on_signal INT TERM HUP

n=0
for k in "${!PL_RUN[@]}"; do
  rid="${PL_RUN[$k]}" a="${PL_ARM[$k]}"
  is_done "$rid" && continue
  [[ -z "$STOP" ]] || break
  if is_paused "$a"; then i="$(arm_index "$a")"; C_SKIPPED[$i]=$(( ${C_SKIPPED[$i]} + 1 )); continue; fi
  reap "$CONCURRENCY"
  [[ -z "$STOP" ]] || break
  if is_paused "$a"; then i="$(arm_index "$a")"; C_SKIPPED[$i]=$(( ${C_SKIPPED[$i]} + 1 )); continue; fi
  if [[ -n "$MAX_USD" ]] && ! budget_gate "$a|${PL_KIND[$k]}" "$((k + 1))" "${PL_KIND[$k]}"; then
    CUTS_JSON="$(jq -c --argjson c "$CUT_JSON" '. + [$c]' <<<"$CUTS_JSON")"; STOP=cut; write_status; break
  fi
  [[ -z "$STOP" ]] || break
  if is_paused "$a"; then i="$(arm_index "$a")"; C_SKIPPED[$i]=$(( ${C_SKIPPED[$i]} + 1 )); continue; fi
  n=$((n + 1)); jid="$(printf 'j%04d' "$n")"
  run_trial "$jid" "$a" "${PL_TASK[$k]}" "${PL_TYPE[$k]}" "${PL_KIND[$k]}" "${PL_TRIAL[$k]}" "$rid" "${PL_YAML[$k]}" "${PL_WD[$k]}" &
  PIDS+=("$!"); PJOB+=("$jid"); PIDX+=("$k")
  i="$(arm_index "$a")"; C_LAUNCHED[$i]=$(( ${C_LAUNCHED[$i]} + 1 )); LAUNCHED=$((LAUNCHED + 1))
  log "launch $rid ($a ${PL_TASK[$k]} ${PL_TYPE[$k]} t${PL_TRIAL[$k]})"
done
reap 1

# --- the batch's end state ---------------------------------------------------------------
total_completed=0 left=0 excluded=0
for i in "${!ARMS[@]}"; do total_completed=$(( total_completed + ${C_COMPLETED[$i]} )); excluded=$(( excluded + ${C_EXCLUDED[$i]} )); done
for k in "${!PL_RUN[@]}"; do is_done "${PL_RUN[$k]}" || left=$((left + 1)); done
paused_n="$(jq 'length' <<<"$PAUSED_JSON")"
if [[ "$ROWS_INVALID" != null ]]; then
  finish failed 3 "failed: the rows file is invalid after $(jq -r '.run_id' <<<"$ROWS_INVALID") ($(jq -r '.error' <<<"$ROWS_INVALID"))"
elif [[ "$DRIFT_JSON" != null ]]; then
  finish failed 3 "failed: drift in $(jq -r '.run_id' <<<"$DRIFT_JSON") ($(jq -r '.field' <<<"$DRIFT_JSON"): expected $(jq -c '.expected' <<<"$DRIFT_JSON"), got $(jq -c '.got' <<<"$DRIFT_JSON"))"
elif [[ "$OUTAGE_JSON" != null ]]; then
  finish partial 1 "$(jq -r '.message' <<<"$OUTAGE_JSON")"
elif [[ "$CUTS_JSON" != '[]' && $left -gt 0 ]]; then
  finish partial 1 "partial (cut max_usd): $((PLAN_N - left)) of $PLAN_N rowed, spent $SPENT"
elif [[ $total_completed -eq 0 ]]; then
  finish failed 3 "failed: no trial completed ($((PLAN_N - left)) rowed, $left without a row)"
elif [[ $paused_n -gt 0 && $left -gt 0 ]]; then
  if [[ "$paused_n" -ge "${#ARMS[@]}" ]]; then
    finish failed 3 "failed: every arm is paused by took-effect ($(jq -c 'keys' <<<"$PAUSED_JSON")); $left trials left"
  fi
  finish partial 1 "partial: paused arm(s) $(jq -c 'keys' <<<"$PAUSED_JSON") left $left trials; --resume --clear-arm <id> after reading the cause"
elif [[ $left -gt 0 ]]; then
  finish partial 1 "partial: $left of $PLAN_N trials have no row (see run.log)"
elif [[ $excluded -gt 0 ]]; then
  finish partial 1 "partial: all $PLAN_N trials rowed, $excluded excluded (transport, infrastructure, interrupted or contaminated)"
else
  finish complete 0 "complete: $PLAN_N trials rowed, spent $SPENT"
fi

tool_use_result.stdout:
fi
  local -a r=("$ROW_BIN" --run-dir "$rd" --task-yaml "$tyaml" --manifest "$MAN_PATH" --attempts "$attempts" --out "$row_out")
  [[ -n "$rr" ]] && r+=(--retry-reason "$rr")
  [[ -n "$PR_OVERRIDE" ]] && r+=(--status "$PR_OVERRIDE")
  "${r[@]}" >> "$plog" 2>&1 || PR_RRC=$?
  return 0
}

run_trial() {  # run_trial <jid> <arm> <task> <type> <kind> <trial> <run_id> <task_yaml> <watchdog_s>
  local jid="$1" arm="$2" task="$3" type="$4" kind="$5" trial="$6" rid="$7" tyaml="$8" wds="$9"
  local base="$BATCH_DIR/$arm/$task-t$trial" tlog="$BATCH_DIR/$arm/$task-t$trial.log"
  local attempt=0 rd="" st="" prc retry_reason="" first_usd=0 sig override="" pid
  local t0 t1
  mkdir -p "$BATCH_DIR/$arm"
  t0="$(date +%s)"
  while [[ $attempt -lt 2 ]]; do
    attempt=$((attempt + 1))
    rd="$(fresh_dir "$base")"
    printf '%s\n' "$rd" > "$JOBS_DIR/$jid.rundir"
    rm -f "$JOBS_DIR/$jid.wd" "$JOBS_DIR/$jid.wdkill"
    printf '%s run-ablation: %s attempt %d run_dir %s\n' "$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)" "$rid" "$attempt" "$rd" >> "$tlog"
    local -a cmd=("$PIPELINE_BIN" --task-yaml "$tyaml" --arm "$arm" --run-dir "$rd" --run-id "$rid" --trial "$trial"
                  --source-tree "$TREE" --suite-file "$SUITE_FILE" --executor "$EXECUTOR" --image "$IMAGE"
                  --docker-bin "$DOCKER_BIN" --max-run-usd "$RUN_CAP")
    # its own process group, so the watchdog can signal the pipeline and everything under it
    if command -v setsid >/dev/null 2>&1; then setsid "${cmd[@]}" >> "$tlog" 2>&1 < /dev/null &
    else "${cmd[@]}" >> "$tlog" 2>&1 < /dev/null &
    fi
    pid=$!
    printf '%s %s %s\n' "$pid" "$(date +%s)" "$wds" > "$JOBS_DIR/$jid.pgid"
    prc=0; wait "$pid" || prc=$?
    rm -f "$JOBS_DIR/$jid.pgid"
    st="$(final_status "$rd")"
    if [[ -f "$JOBS_DIR/$jid.wd" ]]; then
      override=interrupted
      synthesize_record "$rd" "$arm" "$task" "$type" "$trial" "$rid" "watchdog: no final pipeline record after ${wds}s (pipeline exit $prc)"
      break
    fi
    if [[ -z "$st" ]]; then
      override=interrupted
      synthesize_record "$rd" "$arm" "$task" "$type" "$trial" "$rid" "no final pipeline record (pipeline exit $prc)"
      break
    fi
    if [[ "$st" == agent_error ]] && sig="$(is_pipeline_transport_failure "$rd")"; then
      if [[ $attempt -lt 2 ]]; then
        first_usd="$(jq -r '(.spent_usd // 0) | tonumber? // 0' "$rd/meta/pipeline.json" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)"
        retry_reason="transport: ${sig% *} in phase ${sig#* }"
        printf '%s run-ablation: %s %s; retrying once after %ss into a fresh run dir\n' "$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)" "$rid" "$retry_reason" "$RETRY_WAIT" >> "$tlog"
        sleep "$RETRY_WAIT"; continue
      fi
      override=transport_error
    fi
    break
  done
  post_run "$rd" "$rid" "$task" "$tyaml" "$attempt" "$retry_reason" "$st" "$override" "$JOBS_DIR/$jid.row" "$tlog"
  t1="$(date +%s)"
  jq -n --arg rid "$rid" --arg rd "$rd" --argjson att "$attempt" --arg rr "$retry_reason" --arg first "$first_usd" \
    --arg pst "${st:-}" --arg ov "$PR_OVERRIDE" --arg te "$PR_TE" --arg ter "$PR_TE_REASON" --argjson drift "$PR_DRIFT" \
    --argjson grc "$PR_GRC" --argjson rrc "$PR_RRC" --argjson secs "$(( t1 - t0 ))" --argjson extra "$PR_EXTRA" \
    '{run_id: $rid, run_dir: $rd, attempts: $att, retry_reason: (if $rr == "" then null else $rr end),
      first_attempt_usd: ($first | tonumber? // 0), pipeline_status: $pst, override: $ov, took_effect: $te,
      took_effect_reason: $ter, drift: $drift, grade_rc: $grc, row_rc: $rrc, seconds: $secs,
      extra_models: $extra}' > "$JOBS_DIR/$jid.result.tmp"
  mv "$JOBS_DIR/$jid.result.tmp" "$JOBS_DIR/$jid.result"
}

# --- parent: collect a finished job ---------------------------------------------------
append_and_validate() {  # append_and_validate <row-file> <run_id> → 0 ok; 1 invalid (ROWS_INVALID set)
  local rowf="$1" rid="$2" vout vrc=0 n
  local -a v=("$ROW_BIN" --validate "$ROWS"); [[ "$SMOKE" == true ]] && v+=(--allow-ungraded)
  if command -v flock >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    { flock -x 9; cat "$rowf" >> "$ROWS"; vout="$("${v[@]}" 2>&1)" || vrc=$?; } 9>>"$ROWS.lock"
  else
    cat "$rowf" >> "$ROWS"; vout="$("${v[@]}" 2>&1)" || vrc=$?
  fi
  n="$(grep -cF "\"run_id\":\"$rid\"" "$ROWS" || true)"
  if [[ $vrc -ne 0 ]]; then
    ROWS_INVALID="$(jq -cn --arg r "$rid" --arg e "$(printf '%s' "$vout" | tail -1)" '{run_id: $r, error: $e}')"; return 1
  fi
  if [[ "$n" -ne 1 ]]; then
    ROWS_INVALID="$(jq -cn --arg r "$rid" --argjson n "$n" '{run_id: $r, error: "run_id rowed \($n) times"}')"; return 1
  fi
  return 0
}

# apply_flags <arm> <run_id> <took_effect> <reason> <drift> — a took-effect FAIL pauses the
# arm (DEC-0418); the first drift stops the batch (DEC-0407)
apply_flags() {
  if [[ "$3" == fail ]] && ! is_paused "$1"; then
    PAUSED_JSON="$(jq -c --arg a "$1" --arg why "$2: $4" '. + {($a): $why}' <<<"$PAUSED_JSON")"
    log "PAUSED arm $1: $4 (no further trial of $1 launches until --resume --clear-arm $1)"
  fi
  if [[ "$5" != null && "$DRIFT_JSON" == null ]]; then
    DRIFT_JSON="$5"; STOP=drift
    log "DRIFT $2: $5; no further trial launches; the batch fails when the running trials end (DEC-0407)"
  fi
  return 0
}
# record_extra <run_id> <extra models json> — the run's extra models replace its earlier entry
record_extra() {
  EXTRA_RUNS_JSON="$(jq -c --arg r "$1" --argjson e "$2" \
    'if ($e | type) == "object" and ($e | length) > 0 then .[$r] = ($e | map_values(.output_tokens // 0)) else del(.[$r]) end' <<<"$EXTRA_RUNS_JSON")"
}

# outage_tick <run_id> <row status, empty without a row> — the breaker (DEC-0554): consecutive
# collected transport_error trials (collection order, any arm) trip it at $OUTAGE_BREAKER (0 off)
outage_tick() {
  if [[ "$2" == transport_error ]]; then OUTAGE_RUN=$((OUTAGE_RUN + 1)); else OUTAGE_RUN=0; fi
  if [[ "$OUTAGE_BREAKER" -gt 0 && $OUTAGE_RUN -ge $OUTAGE_BREAKER && "$OUTAGE_JSON" == null && -z "$STOP" ]]; then
    STOP=outage
    OUTAGE_JSON="$(jq -cn --arg at "$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)" --argjson n "$OUTAGE_RUN" --arg r "$1" \
      '{at: $at, consecutive: $n, last_run_id: $r,
        message: "partial (outage breaker): \($n) consecutive transport failures; --resume --rerun-status transport_error after the network is back"}')"
    log "OUTAGE breaker: $OUTAGE_RUN consecutive transport_error trials (last $1); no further trial launches (DEC-0554)"
  fi
  return 0
}

collect() {  # collect <jid> <plan-index>
  local jid="$1" k="$2" arm="${PL_ARM[$2]}" rid="${PL_RUN[$2]}" kind="${PL_KIND[$2]}" res="$JOBS_DIR/$1.result"
  if [[ ! -f "$res" ]]; then
    SPENT="$(fadd "$SPENT" "$RUN_CAP")"; ASSUMED_CAP=$((ASSUMED_CAP + 1))
    log "FAILED $rid (the trial job ended without a result; see $BATCH_DIR/$arm/${PL_TASK[$k]}-t${PL_TRIAL[$k]}.log); assumed cap: USD $RUN_CAP charged to spent"
    outage_tick "$rid" ""
    rm -f "$JOBS_DIR/$jid".*; write_status; return 0
  fi
  local first att rr te ter drift
  first="$(jq -r '.first_attempt_usd' "$res")" att="$(jq -r '.attempts' "$res")" rr="$(jq -r '.retry_reason // ""' "$res")"
  te="$(jq -r '.took_effect' "$res")" ter="$(jq -r '.took_effect_reason' "$res")" drift="$(jq -c '.drift' "$res")"
  record_extra "$rid" "$(jq -c '.extra_models // {}' "$res")"
  if [[ "$att" -ge 2 ]]; then
    RETRIES_JSON="$(jq -c --arg r "$rid" --arg why "$rr" --arg u "$first" '. + [{run_id: $r, reason: $why, first_attempt_usd: ($u | tonumber)}]' <<<"$RETRIES_JSON")"
    SPENT="$(fadd "$SPENT" "$first")"; LEDGER_USD="$(fadd "$LEDGER_USD" "$first")"
  fi
  local st="" cost deg pass
  if [[ -s "$JOBS_DIR/$jid.row" ]]; then
    IFS=$'\t' read -r st cost deg pass < <(jq -r '[.status, ((.cost_usd // 0) | tostring), ((.degraded // false) | tostring),
        ((.hidden_test_pass_rate // .defect_catch_rate // "n/a") | tostring)] | @tsv' "$JOBS_DIR/$jid.row")
    if is_rerun "$rid"; then
      # DEC-0553: the new row replaces the old one in place; the old row's reported cost moves to the ledger
      if replace_row_try "$rid" "$JOBS_DIR/$jid.row"; then
        local from ocost
        from="$(jq -r --arg r "$rid" '.[$r].status' <<<"$RERUN_OLD")" ocost="$(jq -r --arg r "$rid" '.[$r].cost' <<<"$RERUN_OLD")"
        LEDGER_USD="$(fadd "$LEDGER_USD" "$ocost")"
        RERUN_LIST="${RERUN_LIST/$'\n'"$rid"$'\n'/$'\n'}"
        RERUN_JSON="$(jq -c --arg r "$rid" --arg f "$from" --arg t "$st" --arg c "$ocost" --arg at "$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)" \
          '. + [{run_id: $r, from: $f, to: $t, old_cost_usd: ($c | tonumber), at: $at}]' <<<"$RERUN_JSON")"
        log "rerun $rid: $from → $st (row replaced in place)"
      else
        ROWS_INVALID="$(jq -cn --arg r "$rid" --arg e "$REPLACE_ERR" '{run_id: $r, error: ("rerun replacement: " + $e)}')"
        log "ROWS INVALID after $rid: $(jq -r '.error' <<<"$ROWS_INVALID")"; STOP=invalid
      fi
    elif append_and_validate "$JOBS_DIR/$jid.row" "$rid"; then :; else
      log "ROWS INVALID after $rid: $(jq -r '.error' <<<"$ROWS_INVALID")"; STOP=invalid
    fi
    DONE_LIST="$DONE_LIST$rid"$'\n'
    account_row "$arm" "$kind" "$rid" "$st" "$cost" "$deg"
    log "done $rid $st pass=$pass USD $cost $(( $(jq -r '.seconds' "$res") / 60 ))m attempts $att${rr:+ ($rr)}"
  else
    SPENT="$(fadd "$SPENT" "$RUN_CAP")"; ASSUMED_CAP=$((ASSUMED_CAP + 1))
    log "FAILED $rid: no row written (ablation-row.sh exit $(jq -r '.row_rc' "$res"); see the trial log); assumed cap: USD $RUN_CAP charged to spent"
  fi
  outage_tick "$rid" "$st"
  apply_flags "$arm" "$rid" "$te" "$ter" "$drift"
  rm -f "$JOBS_DIR/$jid".*
  write_status
}

PIDS=() PJOB=() PIDX=()
watchdog_tick() {
  local j f pid start wds now rd t0
  now="$(date +%s)"
  for j in ${PJOB[@]+"${PJOB[@]}"}; do
    f="$JOBS_DIR/$j.pgid"; [[ -f "$f" ]] || continue
    read -r pid start wds < "$f" 2>/dev/null || continue
    [[ -n "$WATCHDOG_OVERRIDE" ]] && wds="$WATCHDOG_OVERRIDE"
    [[ $(( now - start )) -gt $wds ]] || continue
    rd="$(cat "$JOBS_DIR/$j.rundir" 2>/dev/null || true)"
    [[ -z "$(final_status "$rd")" ]] || continue
    if [[ ! -f "$JOBS_DIR/$j.wd" ]]; then
      printf '%s\n' "$now" > "$JOBS_DIR/$j.wd"
      log "watchdog: $j has no final pipeline record after ${wds}s (twice its phase-sum timeout); SIGTERM to process group $pid"
      kill -TERM -- "-$pid" 2>/dev/null || kill -TERM "$pid" 2>/dev/null || true
    elif [[ ! -f "$JOBS_DIR/$j.wdkill" ]]; then
      read -r t0 < "$JOBS_DIR/$j.wd" || t0="$now"
      if [[ $(( now - t0 )) -ge $WATCHDOG_GRACE ]]; then
        : > "$JOBS_DIR/$j.wdkill"
        log "watchdog: $j still running ${WATCHDOG_GRACE}s after SIGTERM; SIGKILL to process group $pid"
        kill -KILL -- "-$pid" 2>/dev/null || kill -KILL "$pid" 2>/dev/null || true
      fi
    fi
  done
  return 0
}
reap() {  # reap until fewer than $1 jobs run
  local i
  while [[ ${#PIDS[@]} -ge $1 ]]; do
    for i in "${!PIDS[@]}"; do
      if ! kill -0 "${PIDS[$i]}" 2>/dev/null; then
        wait "${PIDS[$i]}" 2>/dev/null || true
        collect "${PJOB[$i]}" "${PIDX[$i]}"
        unset 'PIDS[i]' 'PJOB[i]' 'PIDX[i]'
        PIDS=("${PIDS[@]+"${PIDS[@]}"}"); PJOB=("${PJOB[@]+"${PJOB[@]}"}"); PIDX=("${PIDX[@]+"${PIDX[@]}"}")
        break
      fi
    done
    watchdog_tick
    [[ ${#PIDS[@]} -ge $1 ]] && sleep "$POLL_S"
  done
  return 0
}

on_signal() {
  SIGNALLED=true
  log "interrupted: the driver received a signal; running trials are signalled and will be rerun by --resume"
  STATE=partial; write_status
  exit 1
}

finish() {  # finish <state> <exit> <message>
  STATE="$1"; write_status; log "$3"
  local line
  line="$("$SPEND_BIN" 2>/dev/null | tail -1 || true)"
  {
    printf '%s %s\n' "$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)" "${line:-spend.sh printed nothing}"
    printf '%s batch %s spend USD %s (rows %s + first attempts %s; %s assumed cap charge(s)); max %s\n' \
      "$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)" "$BATCH" "$SPENT" "$ROWS_USD" "$LEDGER_USD" "$ASSUMED_CAP" "${MAX_USD:-none}"
  } >> "$BATCH_DIR/spend.txt"
  echo "run-ablation: $3"
  echo "batch: $BATCH_DIR"
  exit "$2"
}

# --- --rerow: the post-run chain again over a rowed run dir, the row replaced in place ---
# replace_row_try <run_id> <new-row-file> → 0 replaced; 1 with REPLACE_ERR set and the rows file
# untouched (the old row stays). replace_row is the --rerow form: it dies instead
replace_row_try() {
  local rid="$1" newf="$2" tmp="$ROWS.rerow.$$" rc=0 vout="" perr
  REPLACE_ERR=""
  local -a v=("$ROW_BIN" --validate "$tmp"); [[ "$SMOKE" == true ]] && v+=(--allow-ungraded)
  {
    command -v flock >/dev/null 2>&1 && flock -x 9
    perr="$(python3 -I - "$ROWS" "$tmp" "$BATCH" "$rid" "$newf" 2>&1 <<'PY'
import json, sys
rows, tmp, batch, rid, newf = sys.argv[1:6]
new = open(newf, encoding="utf-8").read().strip()
out, n = [], 0
with open(rows, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
    for line in fh:
        try: o = json.loads(line)
        except ValueError: o = None
        if isinstance(o, dict) and o.get("batch") == batch and o.get("run_id") == rid:
            n += 1; out.append(new + "\n")
        else:
            out.append(line if line.endswith("\n") else line + "\n")
if n != 1:
    print("run_id %s has %d rows" % (rid, n), file=sys.stderr); sys.exit(1)
with open(tmp, "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh: fh.writelines(out)
PY
)" || rc=$?
    if [[ $rc -eq 0 ]]; then
      vout="$("${v[@]}" 2>&1)" || rc=$?
      if [[ $rc -eq 0 ]]; then mv "$tmp" "$ROWS"; else REPLACE_ERR="$(printf '%s\n' "$vout" | tail -1)"; fi
    else
      REPLACE_ERR="$(printf '%s\n' "$perr" | tail -1)"
    fi
  } 9>>"$ROWS.lock"
  rm -f "$tmp"
  [[ $rc -eq 0 ]] || { REPLACE_ERR="${REPLACE_ERR:-exit $rc}"; return 1; }
  return 0
}
replace_row() {  # replace_row <run_id> <new-row-file> → 0 replaced; dies (rows file untouched) otherwise
  replace_row_try "$1" "$2" && return 0
  printf '%s\n' "$REPLACE_ERR" >&2
  die "rerow $1: the replacement did not validate or the row moved ($REPLACE_ERR); $ROWS unchanged"
}
rerow_all() {
  local n k rid arm task trial rd tlog newst
  for n in "${!RR_K[@]}"; do
    k="${RR_K[$n]}" rid="${PL_RUN[${RR_K[$n]}]}" arm="${PL_ARM[${RR_K[$n]}]}" task="${PL_TASK[${RR_K[$n]}]}"
    trial="${PL_TRIAL[${RR_K[$n]}]}" rd="${RR_RD[$n]}" tlog="$BATCH_DIR/$arm/$task-t$trial.log"
    printf '%s run-ablation: rerow %s run_dir %s (was %s)\n' "$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)" "$rid" "$rd" "${RR_FROM[$n]}" >> "$tlog"
    rm -f "$WORK/rerow-$n.row"
    post_run "$rd" "$rid" "$task" "${PL_YAML[$k]}" "${RR_ATT[$n]}" "${RR_REASON[$n]}" "$(final_status "$rd")" "" "$WORK/rerow-$n.row" "$tlog"
    [[ -s "$WORK/rerow-$n.row" ]] || die "rerow $rid: ablation-row.sh wrote no row (exit $PR_RRC; see $tlog); $ROWS unchanged"
    replace_row "$rid" "$WORK/rerow-$n.row"
    newst="$(jq -r '.status' "$WORK/rerow-$n.row")"
    record_extra "$rid" "$PR_EXTRA"
    apply_flags "$arm" "$rid" "$PR_TE" "$PR_TE_REASON" "$PR_DRIFT"
    REROWED_JSON="$(jq -c --arg r "$rid" --arg f "${RR_FROM[$n]}" --arg t "$newst" --arg at "$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)" \
      '. + [{run_id: $r, from: $f, to: $t, at: $at}]' <<<"$REROWED_JSON")"
    jq --argjson r "$REROWED_JSON" '.rerowed = $r' "$BATCH_DIR/STATUS.json" > "$BATCH_DIR/STATUS.json.tmp" \
      && mv "$BATCH_DIR/STATUS.json.tmp" "$BATCH_DIR/STATUS.json"
    log "rerow $rid: ${RR_FROM[$n]} → $newst"
  done
  return 0
}

# --- --resume reconciliation: rows on disk are the truth (after --rerow) --------
if [[ "$RESUME" == true ]]; then
  ST_PATH="$BATCH_DIR/STATUS.json"
  STARTED="$(jq -r '.started // empty' "$ST_PATH")"; [[ -n "$STARTED" ]] || STARTED="$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)"
  CUTS_JSON="$(jq -c '.cuts // []' "$ST_PATH")"; RETRIES_JSON="$(jq -c '.retries // []' "$ST_PATH")"
  PAUSED_JSON="$(jq -c '.paused_arms // {}' "$ST_PATH")"
  LEDGER_USD="$(jq -r '.spend.ledger_usd // 0' "$ST_PATH")"; SPENT="$(fadd "$SPENT" "$LEDGER_USD")"
  EXTRA_RUNS_JSON="$(jq -c '.extra_models_by_run // {} | if type == "object" then . else {} end' "$ST_PATH")"
  DRIFT_CLEARED_JSON="$(jq -c '.drift_cleared // []' "$ST_PATH")"; REROWED_JSON="$(jq -c '.rerowed // []' "$ST_PATH")"
  RERUN_JSON="$(jq -c '.rerun // []' "$ST_PATH")"
  OUTAGE_HISTORY_JSON="$(jq -c '.outage_history // []' "$ST_PATH")"
  if [[ "$(jq -c '.outage // null' "$ST_PATH")" != null ]]; then
    OUTAGE_HISTORY_JSON="$(jq -c --argjson o "$(jq -c '.outage' "$ST_PATH")" '. + [$o]' <<<"$OUTAGE_HISTORY_JSON")"
    log "resume: the outage breaker record $(jq -c '.outage' "$ST_PATH") is cleared (kept under outage_history)"
  fi
  if [[ "$CLEAR_PENDING" != null ]]; then
    DRIFT_CLEARED_JSON="$(jq -c --argjson c "$CLEAR_PENDING" '. + [$c]' <<<"$DRIFT_CLEARED_JSON")"
    log "resume: --clear-drift $(jq -r '.run_id' <<<"$CLEAR_PENDING") (previous drift re-read under the current rule: none)"
  fi
  for a in ${CLEAR_ARMS[@]+"${CLEAR_ARMS[@]}"}; do
    if is_paused "$a"; then PAUSED_JSON="$(jq -c --arg a "$a" 'del(.[$a])' <<<"$PAUSED_JSON")"; log "resume: --clear-arm $a (paused arm released)"
    else log "resume: --clear-arm $a: the arm is not paused"; fi
  done
  # rerows first, so spend and per_arm below come from the final rows
  rerow_all
  if [[ -f "$ROWS" ]]; then
    dup="$(jq -R -r --arg b "$BATCH" 'fromjson? | select(type == "object" and .batch == $b) | .run_id' "$ROWS" | sort | uniq -d | head -3 | tr '\n' ' ')"
    [[ -z "$dup" ]] || refuse "resume: $ROWS holds run_id(s) twice: $dup"
    want_ids=$'\n'; for r in ${RERUN_IDS[@]+"${RERUN_IDS[@]}"}; do want_ids="$want_ids$r"$'\n'; done
    rerow_ids=$'\n'; for r in ${REROW_IDS[@]+"${REROW_IDS[@]}"}; do rerow_ids="$rerow_ids$r"$'\n'; done
    want_st=" ${RERUN_STATUSES[*]+"${RERUN_STATUSES[*]}"} "
    while IFS=$'\t' read -r rid st cost deg; do
      k=-1
      for j in "${!PL_RUN[@]}"; do [[ "${PL_RUN[$j]}" == "$rid" ]] && { k=$j; break; }; done
      [[ $k -ge 0 ]] || continue
      if [[ "$want_ids" == *$'\n'"$rid"$'\n'* ]] \
         || { [[ "$want_st" == *" $st "* ]] && [[ "$rerow_ids" != *$'\n'"$rid"$'\n'* ]]; }; then
        # DEC-0553: out of the done set, so the plan launches it again; no counter, no assumed charge;
        # its reported cost (real spend) stays in spent
        [[ "$cost" =~ ^[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?([eE][-+]?[0-9]+)?$ ]] || cost=0
        RERUN_LIST="$RERUN_LIST$rid"$'\n'; SPENT="$(fadd "$SPENT" "$cost")"
        RERUN_OLD="$(jq -c --arg r "$rid" --arg s "$st" --arg c "$cost" '.[$r] = {status: $s, cost: ($c | tonumber)}' <<<"$RERUN_OLD")"
        continue
      fi
      DONE_LIST="$DONE_LIST$rid"$'\n'
      i="$(arm_index "${PL_ARM[$k]}")"; C_LAUNCHED[$i]=$(( ${C_LAUNCHED[$i]} + 1 )); LAUNCHED=$((LAUNCHED + 1))
      account_row "${PL_ARM[$k]}" "${PL_KIND[$k]}" "$rid" "$st" "$cost" "$deg"
    done < <(jq -R -r --arg b "$BATCH" 'fromjson? | select(type == "object" and .batch == $b)

===RUBRIC
# Audit Rubrics

Structured evaluation rubrics for each audit category. Use these to score findings consistently.

## How to Use

1. For each dimension, assess the codebase against the criteria
2. Assign score 1-5 based on the rubric
3. Record reasoning trace explaining the score
4. Calculate category average for overall health

---

## Security Rubrics

### SEC-IV: Input Validation
| Score | Criteria |
|-------|----------|
| 5 | All inputs validated, sanitized, and typed. Allowlist approach used. Schema validation on APIs. |
| 4 | Most inputs validated with minor gaps. Edge cases may lack validation. |
| 3 | Basic validation present but incomplete. Some injection risks remain. |
| 2 | Minimal validation. Clear injection vulnerabilities exist. |
| 1 | No input validation. User input flows directly to sensitive operations. |

### SEC-AZ: Authorization
| Score | Criteria |
|-------|----------|
| 5 | RBAC/ABAC properly implemented. All routes protected. Least privilege enforced. |
| 4 | Authorization present with minor gaps (some routes missing checks). |
| 3 | Basic auth checks but inconsistent. Privilege escalation may be possible. |
| 2 | Weak authorization. Easy bypass or missing on critical routes. |
| 1 | No authorization or completely broken access control. |

### SEC-CI: Confidentiality/Integrity
| Score | Criteria |
|-------|----------|
| 5 | Encryption at rest and in transit. Proper key management. Data classified and protected. |
| 4 | Good encryption with minor gaps. Some sensitive data handling could improve. |
| 3 | Basic encryption but inconsistent. Some data exposure risks. |
| 2 | Weak or missing encryption. Sensitive data partially exposed. |
| 1 | No encryption. Sensitive data in plaintext. Secrets in code. |

### SEC-IN: Injection Prevention
| Score | Criteria |
|-------|----------|
| 5 | Parameterized queries everywhere. No string concatenation in queries. ORM used safely. |
| 4 | Mostly safe with minor gaps in edge cases. |
| 3 | Mixed usage. Some queries parameterized, others vulnerable. |
| 2 | Frequent string concatenation in queries. Clear SQL/NoSQL injection paths. |
| 1 | Pervasive injection vulnerabilities. Eval/exec with user input. |

### SEC-AV: Availability/Resilience
| Score | Criteria |
|-------|----------|
| 5 | Rate limiting, circuit breakers, graceful degradation. DoS protection in place. |
| 4 | Good availability measures with minor gaps. |
| 3 | Basic rate limiting but incomplete. Some DoS vectors remain. |
| 2 | Minimal protection. Resource exhaustion possible. |
| 1 | No availability protection. Trivial DoS attacks possible. |

== DISS-C-001 HIGH None claude-headless anchor: evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:strip_heredocs None
  T: 
  D: Heredoc bodies are removed from the Bash command before the absolute-path scan (check_value, body = strip_heredocs(val)). The rationale assumes a heredoc body is file text being written, but a heredoc is also the standard way to feed commands to an interpreter: `bash <<EOF\ncat /root/hidden/tests.py\nEOF`, `python3 - <<EOF`, `sh <<'X'`. Every path in such a body is executed yet invisible to the outside_path check. Only the hidden/suite/repo substring checks still see the body.
  FM: The agent under test reads hidden tests, the suite directory or other out-of-sandbox paths through a heredoc-fed shell and the run is graded as uncontaminated, corrupting the ablation results the harness exists to protect.

== DISS-C-002 HIGH None claude-headless anchor: evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:check_value None
  T: 
  D: Any Bash word starting with `/.` is skipped as a repo-relative dot-directory reference. ABS_WORD's character class includes `.`, so `/./root/.ssh/id_rsa`, `/../mnt/hidden/x` and `/.//root/x` are all captured as one word and then dropped before `outside()` normalises them. Before this diff these words reached os.path.normpath and SENSITIVE.match and were flagged.
  FM: `cat /./root/secret` or `ls /../mnt/hidden` is a valid shell path to a sensitive location that the grader now ignores, so the contamination flag is bypassed with a two-character prefix.

== DISS-C-003 HIGH None claude-headless anchor: evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:after_closing_quote None
  T: 
  D: A path word immediately preceded by a quote character whose own predecessor is not a separator is treated as the tail of a longer path. An empty quoted string satisfies this: in `cat ""/root/.ssh/id_rsa` the character before the `/` is `"` and the one before that is `"`, which is not whitespace or in "=(<>|;&,", so the word is skipped. The shell expands `""/root/.ssh/id_rsa` to `/root/.ssh/id_rsa`. `''/mnt/hidden/x` works the same way, as does `$x""/root/y` with x unset.
  FM: Prefixing any absolute path with an empty quoted string defeats the outside_path check entirely, for every sensitive root and every multi-component path.

== DISS-C-004 HIGH None claude-headless anchor: evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:HIDDEN_TOKEN None
  T: 
  D: For Bash the hidden check moves from a case-insensitive substring match to the token regex `HIDDEN|(?<=[/._=-])hidden\b|\bhidden(?=[/_=-]|\.[A-Za-z0-9])`. A lowercase `hidden` followed by whitespace, a semicolon or end of string no longer matches, and mixed case (`Hidden`) never matches. `cd hidden; cat test_api.py`, `ls hidden`, `tar cf - hidden | ...`, `cd ../hidden` (lookbehind `/` requires hidden be preceded directly by `/`, which `../hidden` does satisfy, but `cd hidden` does not) all evade. The agent then operates with relative paths that trigger nothing.
  FM: An agent that changes directory into the hidden test tree with a bare `cd hidden` and reads files relatively is graded as uncontaminated, while the pre-diff grader would have flagged it.

== DISS-C-005 MEDIUM None claude-headless anchor: evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:in_quotes None
  T: 
  D: in_quotes decides quoting by parity of all `'` and `"` characters before the position, ignoring escapes, nesting and quote type mixing. Any earlier odd single quote (an apostrophe in a double-quoted string, `echo "it's"`) makes every later one-component sensitive word (`/root`, `/home`, `/mnt`, `/media`, `/srv`) look quoted and skip the check: `echo "don't"; ls -la /root` is not flagged. The same word `/root` on its own is a path candidate.
  FM: Listing or archiving the sensitive single-component roots (ls /mnt, tar -C /root) escapes the contamination flag whenever the command contains a stray apostrophe earlier in the line.

== DISS-C-006 LOW None claude-headless anchor: evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:check_value None
  T: 
  D: `git log --all` / `git reflog` no longer mark a run contaminated, only increment HISTORY_PROBES. The justification is that the sandbox is a fresh git init at the base commit. The grader does not verify that property; if a sandbox is ever created from a clone, a snapshot restore or a mounted source tree with .git, the history-leak control is gone silently. The count is also reset per grade in a module global, and the row schema only carries the count, so a probe never affects verdicts.
  FM: Any future change to sandbox construction that carries history (or an agent that runs `git fetch` from an accessible remote first) reintroduces hidden-answer leakage via history with no grader signal beyond a telemetry integer.

== DISS-C-007 LOW None claude-headless anchor: evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:home_word_outside None
  T: 
  D: In container mode `~/`, `$HOME/` and `${HOME}/` words are no longer scanned at all (HOME_WORD check gated on home_word_outside, and outside() returns False for HOME_PREFIXES before normalising). `~/../../root/x` or `$HOME/../../mnt/hidden` therefore never reach normpath or SENSITIVE.match, whereas the equivalent literal `/home/evaluser/../../root/x` is normalised and flagged.
  FM: A home-relative traversal reaches sensitive roots inside the container without a contamination flag; impact is bounded by what the container actually exposes outside /home/evaluser.

== DISS-C-008 LOW None claude-headless anchor: evals/harness/ablation-row.sh:model_missing None
  T: 
  D: `degraded` now fires only when the requested model is entirely absent from models_used. A phase in which the requested model appears with negligible usage and a different (cheaper or stronger) model produces almost all output tokens is reported as not degraded; the extra model is telemetry only. The same relaxation is applied to the drift guard per the run-ablation.sh header (DEC-0545). Since the batch compares arms, an undetected model substitution biases results.
  FM: A provider-side fallback or a subagent routed to another model that does most of the work passes the degraded and drift checks, and the row is counted as a clean comparison.

### [HIGH-001] Grader: the heredoc regex is exponential on an unterminated heredoc, and the runner has no timeout around the grade

**Criterion:** SEC-AV Availability

**Reasoning Trace:**
> `HEREDOC` is compiled with `re.S`, so `.` in `(?:.*?\n)*?` matches newlines and the inner `.*?\n` and the outer `*?` can split the same run of lines in every composition. When no line matches `\s*\2[ \t]*(?=\n|$)` the engine tries all of them. Measured on the committed pattern with `cat <<EOF` followed by N `line i` lines and no terminator: 16 lines 0.033 s, 18 lines 0.139 s, 20 lines 0.579 s — ×4 per two lines, so 30 lines is about 10 minutes and 40 lines does not finish. ```python
HEREDOC = re.compile(r"<<-?\s*(['\"]?)([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)\1[^\n]*\n(?:.*?\n)*?\s*\2[ \t]*(?=\n|$)", re.S)
```
```bash

```

The trial job never writes its `.result`, the driver's final `reap 1` never returns, no `STATUS.json` finish is written and the concurrency slot is held until the operator kills the driver. **Description:**

HEREDOC = re.compile(r"<<-?\s*(['\"]?)([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)\1[^\n]*\n(?:.*?\n)*?\s*\2[ \t]*(?=\n|$)", re.S)
```
```bash
PR_GRC=0; "${g[@]}" >> "$plog" 2>&1 || PR_GRC=$?
```
**Impact:** One Bash tool_use whose heredoc has no terminator line (a truncated command, `EOF;`, `EOF)`, a here-string followed by more lines, an agent that deliberately writes one) stalls `contamination()` for that trial. The trial job never writes its `.result`, the driver's final `reap 1` never returns, no `STATUS.json` finish is written and the concurrency slot is held until the operator kills the driver. The agent under test controls this input.
**Proof of Concept:**
```
python3 -c 'import re,time; H=re.compile(r"<<-?\s*([\x27\"]?)([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)\1[^\n]*\n(?:.*?\n)*?\s*\2[ \t]*(?=\n|$)", re.S); v="cat <<EOF\n"+"".join(f"line {i}\n" for i in range(20))+"echo done\n"; t=time.time(); H.sub("<<HEREDOC", v); print(time.time()-t)'
# 0.58 s at 20 lines; 2.3 s at 22; 9 s at 24
```
**Remediation:** Drop `re.S` and make each body iteration consume exactly one line so the match is unambiguous: `r"(?<!<)<<-?[ \t]*(['\"]?)([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)\1([^\n]*\n)(?:[^\n]*\n)*?[ \t]*\2[ \t]*(?=\n|$)"` (the lookbehind rejects `<<<`). ### [HIGH-002] Grader: `strip_heredocs` deletes executable text, not only written data

**Severity:** HIGH | **Confidence:** high
**Component:** `head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:1377` (the match includes the header remainder and the body), `:1383` (`HEREDOC.sub("<<HEREDOC", val)` replaces the whole match), `:1415` (`body = strip_heredocs(val)` before the path scan)
**Criterion:** SEC-IV Input Validation

**Reasoning Trace:**
> DEC-0541 says heredoc *bodies* are data. The regex match runs from `<<` through `[^\n]*\n` (the rest of the header line, including any redirect) and the body, and the substitution replaces all of it. So the path scan never sees (a) the header's redirect target, (b) a body fed to an interpreter, (c) a command substitution in an unquoted body. Reproduced against the committed `check_value` logic (head → no hit; base 1.2.0 scan → `outside_path`):
> `cat <<EOF > /root/.ssh/authorized_keys\nkey\nEOF`, `cat <<EOF >> /root/.bashrc\nalias x=y\nEOF`, `bash <<EOF\ncat /root/.ssh/id_rsa\nEOF`, `python3 - <<EOF\nprint(open('/mnt/data/key').read())\nEOF`, `cat <<EOF\n$(cat /root/secret.txt)\nEOF`. The dissent (DISS-C-001 and the rejected gpt-5.5-pro payload) raised the interpreter and substitution shapes; the review raised the redirect shape.

**Description:**
```python
def strip_heredocs(val):
    return HEREDOC.sub("<<HEREDOC", val)
...
        body = strip_heredocs(val)
```
**Impact:** The commonest ways to write a file (`cmd <<EOF > path`) and to run a script (`bash <<EOF`, `python3 - <<EOF`) are invisible to the outside-path check, so a read or write outside the sandbox through them is graded uncontaminated and its row's `hidden_test_pass_rate` enters the arm comparison. The `hidden`/`suite_path`/`repo_name` substring checks still read the full value, so only paths are lost.
**Remediation:** Capture the header remainder as a group and re-emit it (`HEREDOC.sub(r"<<HEREDOC\3", val)` with group 3 = `([^\n]*\n)`); keep the body in the scan when the command word before `<<` is an interpreter (`bash sh zsh python3 python perl ruby node env`) or the delimiter is unquoted (command substitution runs); strip only quoted-delimiter bodies of non-interpreter commands. Add AG-10 rows for each of the five shapes above expecting `outside_path`, and keep the reviewer-prose heredoc row clean.
**References:** CWE-184 Incomplete List of Disallowed Inputs — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/184.html

### [HIGH-004] Grader: an empty quoted string (or `[`, `{`, `:`) before the path defeats `after_closing_quote`

**Severity:** HIGH | **Confidence:** high
**Component:** `head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:1365-1368` (helper), `:1442` (applied)
**Criterion:** SEC-IV Input Validation

**Reasoning Trace:**
> DEC-0557 skips a word whose preceding character is a quote whose own predecessor is not whitespace or one of `=(<>|;&,`. In `cat ""/root/.ssh/id_rsa` the character before `/` is `"` and the one before that is `"`, which passes the test, so the word is dropped; the shell expands `""/root/.ssh/id_rsa` to `/root/.ssh/id_rsa`. Reproduced: `cat ""/root/.ssh/id_rsa`, `cat ''/mnt/secrets/x` → head no hit; base → `outside_path`. The same helper also skips `python3 -c "for p in ['/root/.ssh/id_rsa']: …"` because `[` precedes the quote (review Observation 4, reproduced). Raised by the dissent (DISS-C-003) and the review; confirmed here.

**Description:**
```python
def after_closing_quote(body, pos):   # DEC-0557: "$D"/x → the quote closes a token
    if pos < 2 or body[pos - 1] not in "'\"":
        return False
    before = body[pos - 2]
    return not (before.isspace() or before in "=(<>|;&,")
```
**Impact:** Prefixing any absolute path with `""` or `''` removes it from the scan entirely; absolute paths inside Python list literals in `-c` one-liners are likewise unscanned.
**Remediation:** Require the quoted segment that closes at `pos-1` to be non-empty and to end in a shape that can only be a path head: `$NAME"`, `${…}"`, `)"`, or a segment containing `/`. Add `[`, `{`, `:` to the separator set. AG-10 rows: `cat ""/root/x` → `outside_path`; `"$D"/evals/harness/x` stays clean.
**References:** CWE-184 Incomplete List of Disallowed Inputs — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/184.html
